title: No Memory, No Harness: Why the Database Is the Last Line of Defense — Kay Malcolm, Oracle
talk_summary: Oracle PM argues agent harnesses need shared memory beyond model, tools, and prompt context, because code alone loses intent across teams. She pitches a memory broker backed by a multi-model database to store and retrieve session, episodic, procedural, and semantic memory.

takeaways.technique: Shared memory broker for agent handoffs
takeaways.evidence_quote: they checked in the code but they didn't check in their context from Codeex

takeaways.technique: Single source of truth for heterogeneous memory
takeaways.what_they_do: Store relational, JSON, graph, and vector memory in one database so agents do not reconcile multiple stores or guess which is authoritative.
takeaways.evidence_quote: where is your single source of the truth? The agent has to figure that out

takeaways.what_they_do: Classify memory as short-term, long-term, episodic, procedural, and semantic, then retrieve only the relevant type for the task.
Require context and intent to travel with commits/PRs because git records code but not the reasoning behind it.
takeaways.evidence_quote: git records the code and not human intent

takeaways.technique: Memory tied to branch and commit
takeaways.evidence_quote: figure out which fork and branch it belonged to and which commit it belonged to

takeaways.technique: Avoid per-agent file memory at scale
takeaways.what_they_do: File or chat memory works for one agent but breaks when multiple agents need shared context.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it works with one, but just like in my example, when you scale past one
